texts.setting.cpu_mhz.about: How fast the device's ARM processor runs. The app's own code uses up emulated time at this speed. The first iPhone and the iPhone 3G ran at 412 MHz, the 3GS and the third iPod touch at 600 MHz, and the iPad at 1000 MHz. The system functions that touchHLE provides itself take no emulated time. It is part of the machine.
texts.setting.device_family.about: Which device the app runs on. Auto uses the app's own choice, which is the iPhone unless the app is for the iPad only. An app made for both runs on the device chosen here. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same device.
texts.setting.orientation.about: How the device is held when the app starts. 'App' lets touchHLE decide. It knows which way many games are held and starts them that way, and an app can also turn the device itself. It is part of the machine.
texts.setting.rtc_start.about: The date the device's clock shows when the app starts, in seconds since 1970. For example 1262304000 is 2010-01-01, in the years these apps were made. It cannot be earlier than 2001-01-01, which is the date Apple's clocks count from. After the start the clock runs with the emulated device and never with your computer. It is part of the machine. A game that picks its random numbers from the time plays differently with another date.
texts.slot.game.help: A DECRYPTED .ipa file for iPhone OS 2.x to iOS 4.0. An app downloaded from the App Store is encrypted and does not run. touchHLE's compatibility database (appdb.touchhle.org) lists which apps and versions work.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the app already saved, as Emulator > Export Save Data... wrote it. It is a .zip of the app's Documents and Library folders. They are put back into the app's home folder before the app starts.
